title: Meninges Atlas
subtitle: Explore protective layers, dural reflections, venous sinuses and CSF spaces
altText: Layered sagittal brain illustration showing dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater, subarachnoid space, dural reflections and venous sinuses.
learningObjectives: Identify dura, arachnoid, pia and the clinically relevant meningeal spaces.
Relate dural reflections and venous sinuses to intracranial compartmentalisation and drainage.
Differentiate epidural, subdural and subarachnoid pathology by anatomy and mechanism.

sections.explainSimply: The meninges are three protective coverings wrapped around the brain and spinal cord. Their layers create spaces for blood vessels and cerebrospinal fluid.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Meningeal anatomy matters because haemorrhage, infection, pressure shifts and pain-sensitive structures can alter cognition, behaviour and consciousness even when brain tissue is initially intact.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: The pachymeninx is dura mater; the leptomeninges are arachnoid and pia. Dural border cells permit subdural separation, while the subarachnoid space contains CSF, arteries and bridging veins. Dural folds partition the cranial cavity and house venous sinuses.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of three nested protective sleeves: a tough outer shell, a web-like middle membrane and a delicate inner film that follows every contour.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Headache, altered consciousness and focal deficits may arise from meningeal haemorrhage, inflammation or pressure effects; localisation requires attention to layer and compartment.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Treating all extra-axial bleeding as equivalent obscures different vessels, time courses and emergency risks.
sections.clinicalPearl: The “subdural space” is usually a potential space created by tissue separation, not a pre-existing open cavity.
sections.practicalExample: An older adult with falls and gradually worsening confusion may have a chronic subdural haematoma from torn bridging veins.
sections.limitationsCautions: This atlas supports anatomical learning only; suspected meningitis or intracranial haemorrhage requires urgent medical assessment.

anatomy.label: Dura mater
anatomy.function: Tough outer meningeal layer and pain-sensitive cranial covering
anatomy.inputs: Periosteal attachment and meningeal vascular innervation
anatomy.outputs: Dural folds and venous sinus walls
anatomy.connections: Dural venous sinuses and cranial periosteum
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Helps distinguish arterial epidural bleeding and dural pain sources.

anatomy.label: Arachnoid mater
anatomy.function: Barrier membrane enclosing the CSF-filled subarachnoid space
anatomy.inputs: Interfaces with dura and arachnoid trabeculae
anatomy.connections: CSF pathways and pia via trabeculae
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Its barrier and granulations are central to CSF containment and resorption.

anatomy.label: Pia mater
anatomy.function: Delicate vascular membrane closely investing brain surface
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Inflammation can track along vessels and cortical surfaces.

anatomy.label: Subarachnoid space
anatomy.function: Contains CSF, major arteries, veins and cisterns
anatomy.connections: Basal cisterns, cortical sulci and spinal space
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Blood or infection in this space can distribute widely and irritate meninges.

anatomy.label: Dural venous sinuses
anatomy.function: Drain cerebral veins and receive CSF
anatomy.connections: Falx, tentorium and skull base channels
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Venous outflow obstruction may cause headache, seizures and raised intracranial pressure.
